Jordan: Heads-up — I'm swapping primary for the night shift in ~30. Leaving a sticky kv-cache warmstart that flaked earlier. Leaving notes here so whoever picks up knows the quick fixes.

Maya: Thanks. Are we expecting pager noise?

Jordan: Maybe. p99 for /v1/generate spiked earlier when the cache thrash hit. Customer-visible rate is low but latency SLOs were nudged. I ran the warmstart and it recovered for ~10m then drifted.

Priya: Copy. Are there any open rollouts pinned to the dedicated pool? I can pause traffic to dedicated if we need to shed load.

Jordan: No active rollouts. Traffic routing is default -> try not to change unless we see sustained p99 > 1s. For quick triage: check the KV cache hit ratio and node memory. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.ai/kv-cache-fallback (bookmark).

Luis: If someone gets paged, first step is to toggle the cache-read-only fallback on the runtime. Shortcut (prod):

```
# enable read-only fallback
rctl runtime set cache_mode prod --mode=readonly
# warm restart the worker pool
deployctl restart pool kv-cache-pool --force
```

Jordan: Adding these as quick pointers in case of pager: 1) Check incident-bot alerts in this thread (incident-bot posts below). 2) If multiple hosts show high mem/eviction, scale the pool. 3) If scaling doesn't help, switch model routing to smaller-context variant for the spike window.

incident-bot: [ALERT] 4242424250 - p99 latency for /v1/generate exceeded 900ms in us-east-1. Pager triggered for primary oncall. Links: https://telemetry.redwood.ai/alerts/4242424250

Priya: On it — grabbing the bridge. First, confirming KV eviction rates: `curl -s https://metrics.api/kv/prod | jq .evictions`. Also looking at `cache.hit_ratio` dash.

Maya: If bridge is needed, call: `#oncall-bridge 4242424242` and I'll join. Quick mitigation checklist: 
- fallback to readonly cache (Luis snippet)
- scale kv-cache-pool + workers (x1.5)
- enable model variant routing to `gpt-lite-1` for non-SLA customers
- add temporary rate-limit on unknown heavy routes via gateway

Jordan: Leaving runbook pointers I often use for handoff. Paste these into the handover message so next primary has context: 

> Runbook snippets to copy to next primary: 
> - Command to check hit ratio: `kubectl exec -it cache-proxy-0 -- /bin/metrics.sh hit_ratio`
> - Quick scale: `kubectl scale deployment kv-cache-pool --replicas=6 -n infra`
> - Fallback URL routing toggle: `routesctl set-weight region=us-east model=gpt-neo-1 --weight=0.2`

Luis: Note — the `routesctl` command is guarded; you'll need `ops` group role. If you don't have it, ping @Priya or @Maya.

Priya: I've enabled a conservative autoscale policy window for the pool and bumped min replicas to 4. Watching for evictions to drop.

Jordan: Also leaving a short list of common errors and immediate fixes: 
- `OOM` on cache node -> restart specific pod, check node memory pressure, add swap if persistent.
- `KV_DESYNC` -> quick re-sync job: `jobsctl run kv-sync --namespace infra` (this will rehydrate missing prefixes).
- `HOTSHARD` -> apply shard rebalancer: `shardctl rebalance --shards 8`

Maya: If customers call out degraded latency, use this templated note: 

```
We are currently investigating elevated latency on text generation endpoints. Our engineers are applying cache fallback and scaling measures to restore normal service. We will post updates every 15 minutes or on major milestones.
```

Jordan: Leaving the handoff: primary -> Maya takes over in 30. Secondary -> Priya. My status: reachable on DM and phone. Check `#eng-oncall` for live logs.

Maya: Acknowledged taking primary at 22:40 UTC. I'll monitor p95/p99 and error rates. Priya, if you see persistent evictions after scaling, escalate to infra team.

Priya: Will do. Also, quick snippet to gather per-host mem & eviction for triage: 

```
for host in $(kubectl get pods -l app=kv-cache -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
  echo "-- $host --"
  kubectl exec $host -- bash -lc "cat /proc/meminfo | head -n3; /opt/bin/kv-stats | grep Evictions"
done
```

incident-bot: [INFO] 4242424260 - Auto-scaling triggered for kv-cache-pool: replicas 4 -> 6

Maya: Saw the scale up. p99 dropped to ~720ms briefly. Still above target but trending down. I'll hold primary and watch for 15m.

Jordan: Leaving one last caveat — if p99 doesn't move after scaling & readonly fallback, prepare to route non-critical traffic to `fallback-region` (lower-cost cluster). Use `routingctl region-move --from us-east --to fallback-region --only-non-sla`.

Luis: FYI ops-deploy-bot will log scale events; check `ops-deploy-bot` mentions for the exact deployment IDs.

ops-deploy-bot: Deployment log: kv-cache-pool scaled to 6 replicas by Priya at 4242424262. Change-id: dpl-8b3f2

Priya: I'll update the runbook after the incident with the exact commands I ran. Jordan — thanks for the notes, leaving you a few emoji :thumbsup: in the handoff ping.

Jordan: Thanks all. Passing primary to Maya. If anything noisy, ping @Jordan or page again. :wave:
